newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - January 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - January 16.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- UK JOBLESS TOTAL AT SIX-YEAR LOW

Figures from the Office of National Statistics show that the number of people without work and claiming benefits fell by 45,100 to 1,884,700 in December after adjusting for seasonal patterns. The figures put unemployment in Britain at its lowest level for six years, and the fall, though only half the size of November's record decline, was still larger than expected by City economists.
-- MORGAN GRENFELL IN EMERGENCY TALKS WITH TOP CLIENTS

Following the suspension of top fund manager Nicola Horlick at investment bank Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM) on Tuesday, MGAM executives have held emergency talks with pension fund clients to head off any possible loss of business. Horlick was suspended after allegedly trying to recruit 20 colleagues at MGAM to move with her to the Dutch bank ABN Amro. The emergency talks are aimed at reassuring pension fund clients that operations at MGAM are stable despite the suspension and the deception last year by unit trust manager Peter Young.
-- FORD SET TO SPELL OUT DIMINISHED ROLE FOR HALEWOOD

Motor giant Ford is expected to make an announcement on Thursday morning over the company's intentions for its Halewood factory on Merseyside. Ford is looking to stem losses in its European operations, and the company is expected to tell workers that the new Escort model, due in 1998, will not be built at Halewood. The 'redefining' of Halewood's role is likely to entail substantial job losses at the plant.
-- SECOND RUNWAY APPROVED FOR MANCHESTER AIRPORT

The government has approved the construction of a second runway at Manchester airport in northwestern England, prompting delight among business leaders in the region and anger among environmentalists. Graham Stringer, chairman of Manchester airport, claimed that the second runway will create 50,000 jobs in the region. However, environmentalists have pledged to fight the decision, and have said they will seek a judicial review and that construction of the runway will be opposed on the ground.
-- POWER PRICE REFORM COULD BRING 20 PERCENT CUT

The chairmen of the Electricity Consumers committees have called for radical changes to the way electricity prices are set in England and Wales, claiming that reform could see prices fall by more than 20 percent. The claims are detailed in a paper sent to the department of trade and industry and to Offer, the electricity industry regulator. The consumers committees are concerned about the operation of the Electricity Pool, the body which operates the electricity market in England and Wales.
-- BZW UNITES WITH MoD TO CONQUER GLOBAL MARKETS

The government has provided a grant of 750,000 stg to back a joint venture between the Ministry of Defence and British investment bank BZW to find ways of using military technology to help traders battling in global financial markets. BZW is providing 500,000 stg to the total 1.8 million stg cost of the two-year research programme, which will look at ways of adapting battlefield simulation technology to display on-screen complex movements in asset prices and volatilities in financial markets.
-- FUNDS AT JARDINE FLEMING ARM DROP 10 PERCENT

Figures revealed by Jardine Fleming Investment Management, the first since a trading scandal last August, show that the British business has been among the worst affected. JFIM is the fund management arm of Hong Kong investment bank Jardine Fleming, which discovered last August that a fund manager had been diverting profitable client trades to his own account. Figures released on Wednesday reveal that funds under management at JFIM have fallen 10 percent in the past six months.
-- NORWICH UNION NAMES ITS NEW CHIEF

Norwich Union, the life assurance and general insurance group, has named current finance director Richard Harvey as the company's new chief executive, due to take office from next January. The move clears the way for the 3.5 billion stg flotation of Norwich Union due this summer. Norwich Union will become the first British life assurer to shed its mutual status, as its seeks to raise about 2.0 billion stg to recapitalise its life fund and provide scope for expansion.
-- CORTECS SHARES UP ON SPANISH AGREEMENT

Shares in biotechnology company Cortecs International rose 14p to close at 198.5p on Wednesday following an announcement by the company of a Spanish distribution deal for one of its main products. The agreement, with Ferrer International, is for an oral form of the drug calcitonin, for which could be on sale by 1998 if results from the final stage of clinical trials, due in the next two months, are successful. Ferrer is the leading supplier of calcitonin to Spain, which accounts for about half the 110 million stg European market for the drug.
